newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav customs officials seize huge heroin haul.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav customs officials seize huge heroin haul.

text.p: Yugoslav customs officials seized their biggest single haul of heroin on Friday, confiscating 373 kg (822 pounds) of the drug hidden in a truck on the border with Bulgaria, the state news agency Tanjug reported.
The street market value of the drug was estimated at more than $30 million and was the second major heroin find in two weeks, the federal customs administration was quoted by Tanjug as saying.
The drugs were found in a hidden compartment on a truck with Bulgarian licence plates and driven by a Bulgarian citizen.
In mid-October, customs authorities at the same border seized 190 kg (420 pounds) of heroin concealed among peppers on a Slovenian truck.
Police at the time said it was the biggest single drug shipment discovered at border crossings in former Yugoslavia.

Drug trafficking through former Yugoslavia, once a major east-west thoroughfare for narcotics, had declined before the latest seizures with the breakup of the former federation in 1991, Belgrade authorities said.
